kb.k: Comprehensive VAT Services
kb.q: When do I have to register for VAT?
kb.a: You must register once your VAT-taxable turnover for the previous 12 months goes over £90,000, or if you expect it to go over £90,000 in the next 30 days alone. You can also register voluntarily below the threshold, which can make sense if you mainly sell to VAT-registered businesses.

kb.k: Comprehensive VAT Services
kb.q: How often are VAT returns due?
kb.a: Most businesses file quarterly. Returns and payment are normally due one calendar month and seven days after the end of each VAT period.

kb.k: Comprehensive VAT Services
kb.q: Which VAT scheme is best for me?
kb.a: It depends on your turnover, margins and who your customers are. We’ll compare the schemes using your real figures and recommend the one that saves you the most tax or admin.

kb.k: Comprehensive VAT Services

kb.a: Yes. We’ll bring your records up to date, submit any outstanding returns and help you deal with HMRC about penalties or payment plans.

kb.q: Tell me about P11D & Employee Benefits
kb.a: If you give employees or directors benefits such as a company car, private medical insurance or a loan, HMRC needs a P11D for each of them every year. We value the benefits, prepare and file the P11Ds and P11D(b), and calculate the Class 1A National Insurance you owe.

kb.k: P11D & Employee Benefits
kb.a: P11D and P11D(b) forms must be submitted to HMRC by 6 July after the end of the tax year, and any Class 1A National Insurance must be paid by 22 July if paying electronically.

kb.k: P11D & Employee Benefits
kb.q: What counts as a benefit in kind?
kb.a: Common examples include company cars and fuel, private medical insurance, beneficial loans and accommodation. We’ll review what you provide and tell you what needs reporting.

kb.k: P11D & Employee Benefits
kb.a: Yes. Payrolling most benefits in kind is due to become mandatory from April 2027, replacing most P11D reporting. We can help you move to payrolled benefits in good time.

kb.a: If you work in construction as a contractor or subcontractor, the Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) affects how you pay and how you get paid. We handle CIS registration, subcontractor verification, deductions and monthly returns, and make sure subcontractors reclaim what they’re owed.

kb.k: CIS Services
kb.a: Contractors must file a monthly CIS return by the 19th of each month, covering payments made to subcontractors in the tax month to the 5th.

kb.k: CIS Services
kb.a: Yes. Sole traders reclaim them through their Self Assessment return, and limited companies offset them against their PAYE liability. We make sure nothing is lost.

kb.k: CIS Services
kb.a: Yes. We verify each subcontractor with HMRC so you know the right deduction rate to apply.

kb.q: Tell me about Limited Company Accounts
kb.a: Every limited company must file annual accounts with Companies House and a Corporation Tax return with HMRC. We prepare both, file them on time, and use the figures to show you where your company could be more tax-efficient.

kb.k: Limited Company Accounts
kb.q: When are my company accounts due?
kb.a: For most private limited companies, annual accounts must be filed at Companies House within 9 months of the end of the accounting period. A company’s first accounts can have a different deadline, which we’ll confirm for you.

kb.k: Limited Company Accounts
kb.q: Do you file with both Companies House and HMRC?
kb.a: Yes. We prepare your statutory accounts for Companies House and your Corporation Tax return (CT600) for HMRC, so everything matches.

kb.k: Limited Company Accounts

kb.a: Absolutely. We’ll walk you through the figures, what they mean for your business and how much tax is due, before anything is filed.

kb.k: Corporation Tax Returns Corporation Tax Returns CT600 preparation and filing, plus planning and advice to keep your corporation tax efficient.
kb.q: Tell me about Corporation Tax Returns
kb.a: We calculate your company’s Corporation Tax, prepare and file your CT600 return with HMRC, and make sure you claim every allowance and relief available, so your company pays what it owes and no more.

kb.k: Corporation Tax Returns
kb.a: For most companies, Corporation Tax must be paid 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period, and the CT600 return must be filed within 12 months of the period end.

kb.k: Corporation Tax Returns
kb.q: What rate of Corporation Tax will I pay?
kb.a: The main rate is 25% for profits over £250,000, and the small profits rate is 19% for profits of £50,000 or less. Profits in between pay the main rate reduced by marginal relief. We’ll calculate exactly what applies to your company.

kb.k: Corporation Tax Returns
kb.q: Can you reduce my Corporation Tax bill?
kb.a: Through planning, yes. We make sure every allowable expense and relief is claimed, such as capital allowances and pension contributions, and we review timing before your year end.

kb.a: You don’t file accounts at Companies House, but you must keep accurate records and report your profit on your Self Assessment tax return. Properly prepared accounts make sure you claim every allowable expense.

kb.k: Sole Trader & Partnership Accounts
kb.a: The partnership files its own partnership tax return, and each partner reports their share of the profit on their personal Self Assessment return. We can handle both.

Keep Everything Up to Date : Our team ensures that your business's VAT returns are submitted on time, reducing the risk of penalties, interest charges, or audits. kb.id: p-#s-vat-Different VAT Schemes: Which One Is Right for You?
kb.k: Comprehensive VAT Services Different VAT Schemes: Which One Is Right for You? Different VAT Schemes: Which One Is Right for You?
kb.k2: There are various VAT schemes available in the UK, each suited to different types of businesses and their turnover. Choosing the right scheme can help you optimise your VAT payments and make your accounting process more efficient. Here’s an overview of the main VAT schemes: Standard VAT Scheme This is the default VAT scheme for most businesses. Under this scheme, you charge VAT on your sales and can reclaim VAT on your purchases. Pros : Ideal for businesses with higher VAT-able sales or purchases, allowing you to recover VAT on expenses. Cons : Requires more administrative work to track sales and purchases accurately. Flat Rate VAT Scheme The Flat Rate Scheme is designed for small businesses with a turnover of up to £150,000 (excluding VAT). Under this scheme, you pay VAT based on a flat rate percentage of your gross turnover, which simplifies VAT accounting. Pros : Simplifies VAT calculations by applying a fixed percentage to your turnover. Cons : You cannot reclaim VAT on most purchases (except capital assets over £2,000). Cash Accounting Scheme Under the Cash Accounting Scheme , you only pay VAT on your sales when you receive payment, and you reclaim VAT on purchases when you actually pay your suppliers. This is ideal for businesses with cash flow concerns or slow-paying clients. Pros : You pay VAT on actual cash received, which helps with cash flow. Cons : Can only be used if your VAT taxable turnover is below £1.35 million. Annual Accounting Scheme The Annual Accounting

kb.k: CIS Services What is CIS? What is CIS?
kb.k2: The Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) is a tax deduction scheme that applies to contractors and subcontractors working in the construction industry in the UK. Under CIS, contractors are required to deduct tax at source from the payments they make to subcontractors. The deductions are then passed to HMRC, and subcontractors can claim these deductions back when they file their tax returns. CIS applies to a wide range of construction work, including: Building and construction Demolition Site preparation Installation of electrical and plumbing systems Painting and decorating Contractors are responsible for registering with HMRC and deducting tax from payments made to subcontractors . Subcontractors may have to pay tax upfront, but they can claim it back through their self-assessment or company tax returns.

kb.id: p-#s-corporation-tax-What is a Corporation Tax Return?
kb.k: Corporation Tax Returns What is a Corporation Tax Return? What is a Corporation Tax Return?
kb.k2: A Corporation Tax Return (CT600) is a form that UK limited companies must submit to HMRC detailing their income, expenses, and profits, as well as the tax due on those profits. The Corporation Tax Return: Calculates how much corporation tax your company owes based on the profits made during the financial year. Must be filed annually, typically within 12 months of the end of your company’s financial year. Includes details such as profit and loss , deductions , and taxable income to ensure your company pays the correct amount of tax. Corporation tax is due on your company’s net profits —the total income from sales minus allowable business expenses. Ensuring accurate calculations and timely filings is essential to avoid penalties.
kb.q: What is a Corporation Tax Return?
kb.a:
What is a Corporation Tax Return?

A Corporation Tax Return (CT600) is a form that UK limited companies must submit to HMRC detailing their income, expenses, and profits, as well as the tax due on those profits.

  • Calculates how much corporation tax your company owes based on the profits made during the financial year.
  • Must be filed annually, typically within 12 months of the end of your company’s financial year.
  • Includes details such as profit and loss, deductions, and taxable income to ensure your company pays the correct amount of tax.

kb.k: Management Accounts What are Management Accounts? What are Management Accounts?
kb.k2: Management Accounts are a set of financial reports that provide a detailed view of your company’s financial performance, typically prepared monthly, quarterly, or on any other regular basis that suits your business needs. These reports go beyond the traditional year-end accounts and tax filings, giving you up-to-date information that can guide your decision-making. The typical components of Management Accounts include: Profit and Loss (P&L) Statement : Shows your revenue, expenses, and profits over a specific period, helping you track profitability. Balance Sheet : A snapshot of your company’s assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time, providing insight into your company’s financial position. Cash Flow Statement : Illustrates how cash moves in and out of your business, helping you manage liquidity and plan for future expenses. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) : Customised metrics that are aligned with your business goals and objectives. KPIs track the areas that matter most to your business, such as sales growth, profit margins, and debt levels.

kb.k2: A Self-Assessment tax return is a form submitted to HMRC by individuals who are required to report their income , expenses , and tax liability . This is typically required for people who: Are self-employed Receive rental income Have income from investments or savings Are company directors Earn additional income outside their salary (e.g. freelance work) The tax return will determine how much tax you owe, or if you are due a refund. The deadline for submission is 31st January following the end of the tax year.

This system replaces the traditional paper-based tax reporting process with a fully digital approach , aiming to make tax reporting easier, faster, and more accurate. Under MTD ITSA, taxpayers will need to: Keep digital records of their income and expenses. Use HMRC-approved software to file their tax returns. Submit information to HMRC quarterly rather than annually. Submit a final declaration at the end of the tax year.

This planning is done with the goal of reducing your overall tax liability and optimising the financial position of your business for the upcoming year. In the UK, the tax year typically ends on April 5th for individuals and on March 31st for companies. However, many businesses have a different financial year-end, so it’s essential to start planning well in advance. Some of the key elements of Pre-Year End Planning include: Tax Planning : Taking steps to reduce your taxable income and improve your tax position. Capital Allowances : Identifying opportunities to claim tax relief on business assets. Dividend Planning : Determining the most tax-efficient way to extract profits from your company. Profit and Loss Review : Ensuring that your accounts accurately reflect your business’s financial performance. Pension Contributions : Exploring ways to contribute to a pension scheme for tax relief. Loss Carry-Forward : Evaluating any business losses and how they may be carried forward to offset future profits.
kb.a:
What is Pre-Year End Planning?

Pre-Year End Planning involves reviewing your business’s financial situation before the year-end, identifying opportunities for tax savings, and making strategic decisions to enhance your financial performance. kb.k: Tax Planning Services What is Tax Planning? What is Tax Planning?
kb.k2: Tax planning involves organising your finances and income in a way that legally minimises your tax liabilities. It is not about avoiding tax, but about ensuring that you are taking advantage of available allowances, reliefs, and efficient income structures. Working with an experienced accountant can help you identify opportunities to reduce tax while remaining compliant with the rules set by HM Revenue & Customs . Good tax planning can help you: Reduce unnecessary tax payments Improve cash flow Plan how to take income from your business Take advantage of available tax reliefs Make better long-term financial decisions
kb.a:
What is Tax Planning?

Tax planning involves organising your finances and income in a way that legally minimises your tax liabilities. It is not about avoiding tax, but about ensuring that you are taking advantage of available allowances, reliefs, and efficient income structures.

  • Reduce unnecessary tax payments

  • Plan how to take income from your business
  • Take advantage of available tax reliefs

kb.k: Cloud Software Setup & Support What is Cloud Accounting Software? What is Cloud Accounting Software?
kb.k2: Cloud accounting software is a digital solution that allows you to manage your business’s accounting, bookkeeping, and financial operations over the internet. Unlike traditional software that needs to be installed on your computer, cloud software stores all your data securely in the cloud, accessible anytime, anywhere. The main benefits of cloud accounting include: Accessibility : Access your accounts from anywhere, whether in the office, at home, or on the go. Real-Time Data : View up-to-date financial information at any time, allowing you to make informed decisions quickly. Collaboration : Share data with your accountant, bookkeeper, or business partners in real-time, improving collaboration. Automatic Updates : Cloud software is automatically updated, so you always have the latest features and security patches. Cost-Effectiveness : Cloud software often has flexible pricing plans, saving you on expensive upfront software costs. Popular cloud accounting software options we work with include: Xero QuickBooks Online FreeAgent Sage Business Cloud Accounting

kb.k: Company Secretarial Services What are Company Secretarial Services? What are Company Secretarial Services?
kb.k2: Company Secretarial services are essential for businesses to remain compliant with corporate laws and regulations. These services typically involve tasks related to the governance, record-keeping, and legal responsibilities of a company, including maintaining statutory registers, filing annual returns, and ensuring the company’s operations adhere to relevant laws. A company secretary plays a vital role in managing the company’s legal obligations, ensuring corporate compliance, and acting as a liaison between the company, its shareholders, and regulatory bodies. This can be an invaluable resource, especially for small businesses or companies looking to stay on top of their corporate duties without overwhelming their internal team. Company Secretarial duties may include: Preparation and filing of statutory documents Maintenance of company registers and records Filing annual accounts and returns Coordinating board meetings and minutes Compliance with governance regulations Acting as a point of contact for shareholders and regulatory bodies

kb.k: Company Formation Services What is Company Formation? What is Company Formation?
kb.k2: Company formation is the legal process of registering a business as a limited company with Companies House in the United Kingdom. Once registered, the company becomes a separate legal entity from its owners, meaning the company can enter contracts, own assets, and be responsible for its own liabilities. Forming a limited company offers several advantages, including limited liability protection, potential tax efficiency, and enhanced credibility with clients, suppliers, and investors. The key elements of company formation typically include: Registering the company name Appointing company directors Defining shareholders and share structure Creating the company’s registered office Preparing incorporation documents Registering the company with Companies House Once incorporated, the company must also meet ongoing obligations such as filing annual accounts and submitting confirmation statements.
kb.a:
What is Company Formation?

Company formation is the legal process of registering a business as a limited company with Companies House in the United Kingdom. Once registered, the company becomes a separate legal entity from its owners, meaning the company can enter contracts, own assets, and be responsible for its own liabilities.

  • Registering the company name
  • Appointing company directors
  • Defining shareholders and share structure
  • Creating the company’s registered office
  • Preparing incorporation documents
  • Registering the company with Companies House

kb.k: HMRC Enquiries What is an HMRC Enquiry? What is an HMRC Enquiry?
kb.k2: An HMRC enquiry is a formal investigation or audit conducted by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) into a business's or individual’s tax affairs. HMRC may open an enquiry for several reasons, such as: Random Compliance Checks : HMRC routinely selects businesses for random tax audits to ensure that returns are accurate and tax liabilities are correctly reported. Errors in Tax Returns : If there are inconsistencies, discrepancies, or errors in your tax returns or financial statements, HMRC may open an enquiry to investigate further. Risk-Based Enquiries : HMRC uses risk assessment techniques to identify businesses that may be more likely to underreport income, overstate expenses, or fail to comply with tax regulations. Targeted Investigations : If HMRC suspects fraud or tax evasion, it may launch a more targeted and detailed investigation. There are two main types of HMRC enquiries: Compliance Check : A standard enquiry to verify whether the information provided on your tax returns is accurate and in compliance with tax laws. Full Investigation : A more in-depth examination of your business’s financial records and tax affairs, often involving multiple years of records.
kb.a:
What is an HMRC Enquiry?

An HMRC enquiry is a formal investigation or audit conducted by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) into a business's or individual’s tax affairs.

kb.k: HMRC Enquiries Why HMRC Enquiries Matter Why HMRC Enquiries Matter
kb.k2: HMRC enquiries are an important part of the tax system, ensuring businesses are compliant with UK tax laws and preventing tax fraud. However, they can be stressful, disruptive, and costly if not handled properly. Avoiding Penalties : If your records or tax returns are found to be incorrect, HMRC may impose penalties and interest. It’s essential to respond to HMRC enquiries promptly and correctly to avoid these additional costs. Protecting Your Reputation : An HMRC enquiry can also impact your business’s reputation, especially if there are concerns about your financial integrity. Managing the process properly helps protect your business’s credibility. Tax Liabilities : If HMRC finds that you owe more tax than originally reported, you may face back taxes, interest, and penalties. A thorough investigation and proper guidance can help reduce these liabilities or ensure that you're paying only what’s owed.

Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (MTD ITSA) is the biggest change to Self Assessment in decades. Instead of one tax return a year, many sole traders and landlords must keep digital records and send HMRC a short update every quarter. Here’s what it means and when it affects you.

kb.k: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: What Sole Traders and Landlords Need to Know Who is affected, and when Who is affected, and when
kb.k2: MTD for Income Tax is being introduced in stages, based on your qualifying income : your combined gross self-employment and UK property income, before expenses. From April 2026: qualifying income over £50,000 From April 2027: qualifying income over £30,000 From April 2028: qualifying income over £20,000 HMRC usually looks at the tax return from two years earlier to decide whether you’re in. Employment income, pensions and dividends don’t count towards the threshold.
kb.a:
Who is affected, and when

MTD for Income Tax is being introduced in stages, based on your qualifying income: your combined gross self-employment and UK property income, before expenses.

  • From April 2026: qualifying income over £50,000
  • From April 2027: qualifying income over £30,000
  • From April 2028: qualifying income over £20,000
links: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: What Sole Traders and Landlords Need to Know

kb.q: Sole Trader or Limited Company? How to Choose the Right Structure
kb.a:
Sole Trader or Limited Company? How to Choose the Right Structure

One of the most common questions we hear is whether to stay a sole trader or set up a limited company. There is no one-size-fits-all answer: the right structure depends on your profits, plans, risk and how you want to take money out of the business.
links: Sole Trader or Limited Company? How to Choose the Right Structure

kb.k: Sole Trader or Limited Company? How to Choose the Right Structure Sole trader: simple and flexible Sole trader: simple and flexible
kb.k2: Easy and free to set up, with minimal paperwork Profits taxed through Self Assessment with Income Tax and National Insurance You and the business are legally the same, so you’re personally liable for debts Will fall under Making Tax Digital for Income Tax if your income is over the thresholds
kb.a:
Sole trader: simple and flexible

  • Easy and free to set up, with minimal paperwork
  • Profits taxed through Self Assessment with Income Tax and National Insurance
  • You and the business are legally the same, so you’re personally liable for debts
  • Will fall under Making Tax Digital for Income Tax if your income is over the thresholds
links: Sole Trader or Limited Company? How to Choose the Right Structure

kb.k: Sole Trader or Limited Company? How to Choose the Right Structure Limited company: separate and scalable Limited company: separate and scalable
kb.k2: The company is a separate legal entity, which limits your personal liability Profits pay Corporation Tax: 19% up to £50,000 and 25% above £250,000, with marginal relief in between You can take a mix of salary and dividends, which can be more tax-efficient at higher profits More admin: annual accounts, a confirmation statement, Corporation Tax returns and identity verification at Companies House
kb.a:
Limited company: separate and scalable

  • The company is a separate legal entity, which limits your personal liability
  • Profits pay Corporation Tax: 19% up to £50,000 and 25% above £250,000, with marginal relief in between
  • You can take a mix of salary and dividends, which can be more tax-efficient at higher profits
  • More admin: annual accounts, a confirmation statement, Corporation Tax returns and identity verification at Companies House
links: Sole Trader or Limited Company? How to Choose the Right Structure

kb.k: Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know
kb.k2: Congratulations on forming your company! The first year brings a handful of new responsibilities, and most problems we see come from simply not knowing what’s due and when. Here’s a clear run-through of the essentials.
kb.q: Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know
kb.a:
Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know

Congratulations on forming your company! The first year brings a handful of new responsibilities, and most problems we see come from simply not knowing what’s due and when. Here’s a clear run-through of the essentials.
links: Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know

kb.k: Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know Your key responsibilities Your key responsibilities
kb.k2: Identity verification: since 18 November 2025, directors and people with significant control must verify their identity with Companies House. Register for Corporation Tax within three months of starting to trade. Set up payroll if you’ll pay yourself or anyone else a salary. Keep company money separate in a business bank account. Keep statutory registers and record board decisions, including dividends.
kb.a:
Your key responsibilities

  • Identity verification: since 18 November 2025, directors and people with significant control must verify their identity with Companies House.
  • Register for Corporation Tax within three months of starting to trade.
  • Set up payroll if you’ll pay yourself or anyone else a salary.
  • Keep company money separate in a business bank account.
  • Keep statutory registers and record board decisions, including dividends.
links: Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know

kb.k: Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know Your first-year deadlines Your first-year deadlines
kb.k2: Confirmation statement: at least once a year Annual accounts: your first accounts are usually due 21 months after incorporation Corporation Tax return (CT600): 12 months after your accounting period ends Corporation Tax payment: usually 9 months and 1 day after the period ends
kb.a:
Your first-year deadlines

  • Confirmation statement: at least once a year
  • Annual accounts: your first accounts are usually due 21 months after incorporation
  • Corporation Tax return (CT600): 12 months after your accounting period ends
  • Corporation Tax payment: usually 9 months and 1 day after the period ends
links: Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know

kb.k: Your First Year as a Limited Company Director: What You Need to Know Taking money out Taking money out
kb.k2: As a director you can take a salary, dividends from profits after tax, or borrow through a director’s loan account. Each has different tax rules, and getting the mix wrong can be costly. We plan this with you at the start of the year, not the end.

kb.q: How to put yourself in the strongest position
kb.a:

  • File your tax returns early so the latest year’s figures are available
  • Keep business and personal finances separate
  • Avoid big unexplained transfers in the months before applying
  • Talk to your accountant before reducing profits through expenses or pension contributions in the year you apply
  • Use a mortgage adviser who understands self-employed income

Right to be informed : to receive clear information about how we use your personal information, which is what this policy provides. Right to rectification : to ask us to correct information that is inaccurate or complete information that is incomplete. Right to erasure : to ask us to delete your information. Right to restrict processing : to ask us to limit how we use your information, for example while we check its accuracy. Right to object : to object to us using your information where we rely on legitimate interests, and to object at any time to direct marketing. Right to data portability : to receive information you have given us in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format, or to ask us to send it to another organisation. Rights relating to automated decision-making : we do not make decisions about you based solely on automated processing that have legal or similarly significant effects. Electronic identity checks are always reviewed by a person. Right to withdraw consent : where we rely on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time. This does not affect anything we did before you withdrew

kb.k: Cookie Policy What Are Cookies? What Are Cookies?

kb.k: Data Protection Policy The Data Protection Principles The Data Protection Principles
kb.k2: We follow the seven principles set out in Article 5 of the UK GDPR. Personal information must be: Processed lawfully, fairly and transparently : we only use personal information where we have a lawful basis, and we tell people how we use it through our Privacy Policy and engagement letters. Collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes : we only use information for the purposes we collected it for, or for compatible purposes allowed by law. Adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary : we only ask for the information we genuinely need to provide our services and meet our legal obligations. Accurate and kept up to date : we take reasonable steps to correct inaccurate information and ask clients to tell us about changes. Kept for no longer than necessary : we follow our retention schedule and securely delete information we no longer need. Kept secure : we use appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect information against loss, misuse and unauthorised access. Accountability : we take responsibility for complying with these principles and keep records to show how we do so.

kb.k: Data Protection Policy Confidentiality and Professional Duties Confidentiality and Professional Duties
kb.k2: As accountants and bookkeepers, we owe our clients a professional duty of confidentiality in addition to our obligations under data protection law. We will not disclose client information to anyone outside Zen unless: the client has authorised it; it is necessary to provide our services, for example filing with HMRC or Companies House; we are required to by law or by our regulator; or it is necessary to protect our legitimate interests, for example in responding to a legal claim. Under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, the Terrorism Act 2000 and the Money Laundering Regulations, we must report knowledge or suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing to the National Crime Agency. These legal duties override confidentiality, and we must not tell anyone that a report has been made.
kb.a:

As accountants and bookkeepers, we owe our clients a professional duty of confidentiality in addition to our obligations under data protection law.

  • the client has authorised it;
  • it is necessary to provide our services, for example filing with HMRC or Companies House;
  • we are required to by law or by our regulator; or
  • it is necessary to protect our legitimate interests, for example in responding to a legal claim.

kb.k: Data Protection Policy Data Breaches Data Breaches
kb.k2: A personal data breach is any breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal information. Examples include an email sent to the wrong person, a lost laptop or a hacked account. Report : anyone who discovers or suspects a breach must report it to Ann Williams immediately. Contain : we act quickly to limit the damage, for example by recalling an email, resetting passwords or wiping a lost device. Assess : we assess the risk to the individuals affected. Notify the ICO : where a breach is likely to result in a risk to people’s rights and freedoms, we report it to the ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware of it. Tell those affected : where a breach is likely to result in a high risk to individuals, we tell them without undue delay and explain what they can do to protect themselves. Record and learn : we record every breach, whether or not it is reported, and take steps to stop it happening again.
kb.a:

  • Contain: we act quickly to limit the damage, for example by recalling an email, resetting passwords or wiping a lost device.
  • Assess: we assess the risk to the individuals affected.
  • Notify the ICO: where a breach is likely to result in a risk to people’s rights and freedoms, we report it to the ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.

kb.k: About Zen Why Zen Bookkeeping & Advisory Why Zen Bookkeeping & Advisory
kb.k2: Zen Bookkeeping & Advisory was founded with a clear purpose: to go beyond the traditional accountant-client relationship . For many people, working with an accountant can feel distant or transactional. Communication may only happen once a year at tax time, financial reports can be confusing, and advice is often reactive rather than proactive. This can leave business owners and individuals feeling disconnected from their own numbers. At Zen, we do things differently. We provide financial support that is collaborative, approachable, and genuinely helpful —guiding you through your numbers, offering proactive advice, and helping you plan for the future with confidence. To make our support even more comprehensive, we have built partnerships with trusted professionals , including mortgage advisors, financial planners, and Chartered Certified Accountants. This allows us to provide a one-stop shop for all your accountancy and financial advisory needs , giving you access to expert guidance across personal and business finances without the stress of managing multiple providers. With Zen, it’s not just about numbers—it’s about building a financial partnership that simplifies your life, protects your interests, and helps you achieve your goals .

We exist to simplify complexity —turning confusing numbers, tax regulations, and financial obligations into clear, actionable insights that help our clients make informed decisions. By providing accurate, timely bookkeeping and advisory support, we give our clients the freedom to focus on what truly matters: growing their business, pursuing their goals, and building the life they envision. Our mission goes beyond traditional accounting. We aim to create long-term partnerships with our clients, offering guidance and advice that is proactive, personalised, and tailored to their unique circumstances. Whether helping a startup find its footing, a small business navigate growth, or an individual plan for a secure financial future, we are committed to delivering support that is practical, reliable, and focused on real outcomes. Ultimately, our mission is to empower every client— businesses and individuals alike —to take control of their finances, make confident decisions, and feel supported every step of the way. With Zen Bookkeeping & Advisory, managing your finances becomes less of a burden and more of a foundation for success.
